title: removeCollateralWLpTo does not verify tokenId belongs to the position unless the removal empties the NFT, letting any position owner unwrap LP and harvest rewards from other positions' wLp NFTs
description: Discovery: Q3.1/Q3.2 (paired-operation consistency), MODIFIER-01 sibling diff. harvestTo() and getCollWLpAmt() both check that _tokenId is in __posCollInfos[_posId].ids[_wLp], but removeCollateralWLpTo() only checks membership inside the `newWLpAmt == 0` branch (ids.remove(...) returns false -> NOT_CONTAIN). For a partial removal (0 <= _amt < balanceOfLp) or _amt == 0 there is no check that the token belongs to _posId. PosManager is the ERC721 owner of every collateralized wLp NFT, so wLp.unwrap(tokenId, amt, receiver) and wLp.harvest(tokenId, ...) (both onlyOwner(id) in the mock wLp) succeed for any tokenId held by PosManager. InitCore.decollateralizeWLp only checks onlyAuthorized(_posId) for the caller's own position, whitelisted wLp and mode status, then the health check runs on the caller's own (unchanged) position.
root_cause: Position-to-token ownership is only enforced on the full-removal path; the partial/zero path trusts the caller-supplied (_wLp, _tokenId) pair and operates on the globally-owned NFT balance (balanceOfLp is per tokenId, not per position).

harm.who: any position owner who collateralized a wLp NFT (e.g. a Uniswap-V2 LP wrapper)
harm.loses_what: all but 1 unit of the LP tokens underlying the NFT, plus all accrued wLp rewards
harm.magnitude: up to balanceOfLp(tokenId) - 1 per victim NFT; victim position can also become liquidatable

exploit_trace: 1. Victim collateralizes wLp NFT id=N (balanceOfLp = 1000 LP) in position V; PosManager owns NFT N.
2. Attacker creates own position A (any healthy or empty position) and calls InitCore.decollateralizeWLp(A, wLp, N, 999, attacker).
3. onlyAuthorized(A) passes; wLp is whitelisted; PosManager.removeCollateralWLpTo(A, wLp, N, 999, attacker): newWLpAmt = 1000 - 999 = 1 != 0, so the NOT_CONTAIN membership check is skipped.
4. _harvest(A, wLp, N) sends N's pending rewards to PosManager and credits pendingRewards[A][token]; wLp.unwrap(N, 999, attacker) is called by PosManager (the owner) and sends 999 LP to the attacker.

5. ensurePositionHealth(A) checks only A, which is unchanged, so the call succeeds. Attacker later calls claimPendingRewards(A, tokens, attacker) to collect the stolen rewards; with _amt = 0 only the rewards are stolen.

preconditions.text: a whitelisted wLp has at least one NFT collateralized by another position

postconditions.text: victim position holds an NFT with ~0 LP backing and may be undercollateralized

rules_applied: R10:✓(worst state: full NFT balance minus 1)
R12:✓(only enabler is any collateralized NFT)
depth_evidence: [BOUNDARY:_amt=0 -> newWLpAmt=balance != 0, no membership check, harvest of foreign token]
postconditions_created: victim NFT balance drained to 1 unit

title: Liquidation of a position with health == 0 reverts with division by zero in LiqIncentiveCalculator, contradicting the explicit underwater bypass in InitCore
description: Discovery: Q5.6 (math boundary check), Q4.6, ECON-02. getPosHealthCurrent_e18 returns 0 when collateral credit is 0 while borrow credit > 0 (for example every collateral token has collFactor 0, or collateral dust whose credit floors to 0). InitCore.liquidate/liquidateWLp explicitly handle `vars.health_e18 == 0` as the underwater case (`if (vars.health_e18 != 0) _ensurePosHealthAfterLiq`), but before that they pass health_e18 to getLiqIncentiveMultiplier_e18, which computes (ONE_E18 * ONE_E18) / _healthFactor_e18 with no zero guard and panics.
root_cause: The incentive calculator assumes health_e18 > 0 while the caller treats health_e18 == 0 as a valid, liquidatable underwater state.

harm.loses_what: bad debt on fully underwater positions cannot be cleared by liquidators and stays in totalDebt, inflating the reported share price until withdrawals fail on cash
harm.magnitude: entire remaining debt of every position whose collateral credit is 0

exploit_trace: 1. Governor sets collFactor_e18 = 0 for a collateral pool (config has no remover) or a position's collateral shrinks until credit floors to 0 while debt remains.
2. getPosHealthCurrent_e18(posId) returns 0 (< ONE_E18, so POSITION_HEALTHY check passes).
3. Liquidator calls InitCore.liquidate(posId, ...) -> _liquidateInternal repays debt -> getLiqIncentiveMultiplier_e18(mode, 0, ...) executes 1e36 / 0 and reverts with Panic 0x12.
4. The position cannot be liquidated at any price; the debt remains outstanding.

preconditions.text: position collateral credit is exactly 0 while debt > 0

postconditions.text: unliquidatable bad debt remains in the pool

rules_applied: R12:✓(enablers: collFactor=0, dust collateral, collateral fully seized)

title: updatePosDebtShares snapshots lastDebtAmt with the pre-update debt ratio, so a second debt update in the same timestamp underflows and reverts (repay/borrow/liquidate DoS)
description: Discovery: Q2.2/Q7.5 (stale state, cross-tx rounding), Q5.6. updatePosDebtShares assumes `debtAmtCurrent >= extraInfo.lastDebtAmt` (NOTE comment) and does `debtAmtCurrent - extraInfo.lastDebtAmt` with checked math. lastDebtAmt is computed as ceil(newDebtShares * totalDebt / totalDebtShares) using the ratio BEFORE the pool's repay/borrow runs (InitCore calls updatePosDebtShares first, then pool.repay/pool.borrow). Pool.repay rounds the repaid amount UP and pool.borrow rounds shares UP, so the post-operation ratio is slightly lower, leaving lastDebtAmt up to 1 wei above the position's real debt. Any further updatePosDebtShares for that position in the same block timestamp (no interest accrued yet) reverts with an arithmetic underflow.
root_cause: Interest-tracking snapshot uses a pre-operation ratio while the pool applies round-up arithmetic afterwards; the invariant debtAmtCurrent >= lastDebtAmt is not preserved.

harm.loses_what: a second repay/borrow/liquidation touching the same position and pool in the same block reverts (e.g. repay then borrow in one multicall, or a liquidation in the block after the borrower or another large borrower changed debt)
harm.magnitude: liveness only, per-block; larger debts self-heal after one second of accrual, small-debt positions can stay blocked several seconds

exploit_trace: 1. Pool: totalDebt = 1,000,000, totalDebtShares = 900,000; sole borrower position P holds all 900,000 shares.

2. P (or anyone authorised) repays 1 share: _repay -> updatePosDebtShares sets lastDebtAmt = ceil(899,999 * 1,000,000 / 900,000) = 999,999; then pool.repay charges ceil(1.111..) = 2 so totalDebt = 999,998, shares = 899,999.

3. In the same block (same timestamp, no accrual) a second repay/borrow/liquidate on P calls updatePosDebtShares: debtAmtCurrent = 999,998, lastDebtAmt = 999,999, so 999,998 - 999,999 underflows and the tx reverts.
4. A borrower can front-run a liquidator's tx in the same block with a dust repay/borrow to make that liquidation revert for the block.

preconditions.text: two debt updates for the same position/pool in the same block timestamp, debt ratio non-integral

postconditions.text: position cannot be updated until a timestamp with at least 1 wei of accrued interest

rules_applied: R8:✓(cached lastDebtAmt snapshot across multi-step ops)
R12:✓(enablers: same-timestamp second op, rounding up in repay/borrow)
depth_evidence: [BOUNDARY:totalDebt=1,000,000 shares=900,000 repay 1 share -> lastDebtAmt 999,999 vs current 999,998]
postconditions_created: temporary per-block DoS of the position

title: InitOracle fallback does not work for an unset or malformed source: try/catch does not catch ABI-decode failure, so getPrice_e36 reverts even when the other source is valid
description: Discovery: Q6.3/Q4.2, ORC-02. The comments state that if one of the sources is invalid the other is used. primarySources[_token]/secondarySources[_token] default to address(0). A call to address(0) returns success with empty returndata, the return value decode then fails in the calling contract, which a catch clause does not intercept (it only catches reverts of the callee), so the whole getPrice_e36 reverts. Both sources must therefore be set for every priced token, and maxPriceDeviations_e18 must be non-zero (default 0 makes the deviation check always revert when both are valid). The same applies to a primary that returns malformed data.
root_cause: try/catch around an external call to a possibly-empty address does not provide the documented single-source fallback.

harm.who: borrowers and liquidators of any token configured with only one oracle source
harm.loses_what: borrow, collateral valuation and liquidation for positions holding that token revert (position health cannot be computed)
harm.magnitude: all positions using that token while only one source is configured

exploit_trace: 1. Governor sets only primarySources[T] (secondary left at address(0)).
2. Any call to getPrice_e36(T) executes the secondary try on address(0); decode of empty returndata reverts in InitOracle, not caught.
3. getPosHealthCurrent_e18 for any position holding T reverts, blocking borrow, decollateralize and liquidation.

preconditions.text: one source unset or returning malformed data

audit_trail.missing_precondition: governance must configure only one source
